question: When assistant referees got offside wrong at the 2002 World Cup, which mistake was most common?
answer: Flagging attackers who were onside. About 26% of offside situations were judged wrongly, and most errors were raised flags. A forward in motion is seen slightly ahead of where he really is when the pass is struck, so level looks beyond. The attack that was wrongly stopped leaves nothing to replay.
move: The mistakes that end the story are the ones nobody sees on the replay.
trap: Recalling goals given from offside, which are replayed endlessly.

diagram.caption: About one offside call in four was wrong, mostly flags raised against onside attackers.

source: Helsen et al., Journal of Sports Sciences, 2006
reference: Helsen, Gilis & Weston, Errors in judging offside in association football: test of the optical error versus the perceptual flash-lag hypothesis, Journal of Sports Sciences, 2006
